validity.researcher_notes: CLASSIFICATION / duplicate check against the 44-row roster: P7769 is NOT a duplicate of P0177 (Ville Platte->Louisiana, 99.3 mi -- the pre-existing Line 100 mainline, certificated separately in April 2019 per FERC order fn.5), P3282 (Ragley->Louisiana, 36.9 mi -- this is exactly 'the approximately 36.9-mile Line 200 pipeline' the FERC order describes as Construction Phase 1), or P7770 (32.4 mi, cap 4600 -- 'the remainder of Line 300' plus the first Indian Bayou compressor, Construction Phase 2 pipe). P7769 corresponds specifically to 'Operational Phase 3': per the FERC order (pp.4-5), Construction Phase 2 facilities are 'the remainder of Line 300; one additional electric motor-driven compressor at the Indian Bayou Compressor Station to provide an additional 52,800 hp ... resulting in a project total of 211,200 hp'; the order states 'after the installation of the Construction Phase 2 compression, targeted to be available for service in late 2026, the project's nominal transportation capacity will be 5,400,000 Dth/d ... (Operational Phase 3)'. So P7769 is the FINAL COMPRESSOR UNIT ONLY -- zero new pipe, zero new diameter. LengthKnown=0/Diameter=blank is therefore CORRECT and is the batch's documented convention for compression-only expansions, not an error. Independent confirmation beyond the FERC order text: the EIA dated release contemporaneous with the sheet's own 2025-10-06 update (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Oct2025.xlsx) also shows miles='na' and diameter blank for this exact project row -- EIA itself treated this as a no-new-mileage row at that time. EIA's LATER vintages (2026-01 onward) restate miles=69.3/diameter=42 on this same row, which is the project's AGGREGATE Line 200+300 mileage (36.9+32.4=69.3, matching P3282+P7770 combined) -- almost certainly an EIA data-entry conflation of the aggregate onto the Phase-3 line starting 2026-01, not a real scope change (aggregate-vs-segment rule: a SYSTEM figure is never a valid ref for this SEGMENT cell). Flagging for awareness; not something to fix in GEM's row.

UNRESOLVED CONFLICT, not fully reconciled -- flagging clearly rather than picking a winner. Three genuinely different dates appear across the evidence trail for this specific Phase-3/final-compressor increment: (1) the ORIGINAL 2023-04-21 FERC order targeted 'late 2026' for Operational Phase 3; (2) Driftwood's own Nov-2024 FERC filing (docket CP21-465-004) requested the regulatory deadline be pushed to 2027-10-21, citing litigation delays and the then-pending Woodside-Tellurian-related ownership uncertainty; (3) EIA's Oct-2025 vintage (matching the sheet) shows 2028; (4) EIA's Jan-2026 vintage shows 2027; (5) EIA's May-2026 and Aug-2026 vintages both show 2029. Points (4) and (5) are the SAME EIA vintages that started restating this row's mileage as 69.3 mi (the project aggregate) instead of blank/na -- since that mileage change is judged (see validity[] classification entry) to reflect an EIA row-level data problem rather than a real re-scoping, I am NOT treating EIA's 2027/2029 restatements as more authoritative than the Oct-2025 figure that matches the sheet. On balance I lean toward keeping 2028, but this is a judgment call under genuine uncertainty, not a clean confirmation -- a future pass should look for a definitive FERC order granting/denying the Oct-2027 extension request (none found; only the request itself was located) and any newer Williams/Woodside disclosure that states an explicit in-service date for the Indian Bayou compressor addition specifically.
